A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, references, and Appendices A–C. The revised theoretical material and relocated appendix displays can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v5 reports original language-model fine-tuning experiments in Section 5 and Appendix B, including training losses, generation scores, and KL-divergence results.

after.justification: v6 retains those original experiments and their outcomes in Tables 1–3 and Figures 4–10.

M1.justification: The token-tree pruning and Huffman compression procedure in Definition 3.3, training objectives, and forward/inverse alignment procedures are unchanged. The revision changes theoretical assumptions and derivations rather than an algorithm or model architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use Alpaca, TruthfulQA, Beavertails, and IMDb for the same alignment, generation, and safety studies. The appendix experiments, including reversed fine-tuning scenarios, are retained.

E2.justification: The forward-versus-inverse alignment comparisons retain the same participants. Appendix B.2 and Figure 7 retain PPO, DPO, KTO, and SimPO, with no comparator added or removed.

E3.justification: The reported splits, snapshot comparisons, model configurations, sample sizes, and scoring procedures are unchanged. This includes the one-epoch resistance experiment and Appendix B.2's KL-divergence threshold of 0.01.

E4.justification: The same analyses test alignment algorithms, alternative KL metrics, reversed fine-tuning directions, model size, and pre-training volume. Appendix B contains no added or removed ablation or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the standard-deviation shading described in Figures 5–6. No run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the plotted results in Figures 4–10 are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains Llama2-7B's unsafe-data counts of 961, 844, 801, and 729. The reported resistance, rebound, and scaling trends also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorems 4.2/A.8 replace the independent-dataset setup with pre-training comprising three equal-cardinality components, with alignment and perturbation matching two component distributions. Appendix A replaces the corresponding derivation with mixture-based integrals, Taylor expansions, and a permutation-based sign argument. Definition 4.1 drops pairwise disjointness, and Definition A.3 adds multiplication by the number of leaves. These substantially revise the central theoretical foundation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about resistance, rebound, inverse dataset-size dependence, and stronger elasticity with increased model size and pre-training volume. The revised theorem assumptions are not accompanied by narrowed headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 now motivates alignment distributions as already represented within the broad pre-training corpus, replacing the previous distinct-and-independent account. This changes the explanation of the theoretical setting; the experimental interpretations, Section 6.1 limitations, and Appendix C discussions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, data preparation descriptions, and the model-weight/code availability statement are unchanged. The expanded appendix supplies mathematical reasoning without adding reproduction settings or access information.

R1.justification: The cited-work set, Section 2 related-work discussion, and Appendix C.1 positioning relative to transfer learning are unchanged. No substantive novelty or prior-work relationship is revised.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to Section 4.1 and Appendix A, including dataset terminology, proof exposition, and changing 'Shannon entropy' to 'cross-entropy' in Lemma A.5. The broader narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The expanded proof changes equation layout and reflows the appendices, repositioning existing displays such as Figure 7, Table 3, and Figure 10. All ten figures and three tables retain their content and designs.

improvement.justification: v6 fixes Definition A.3's scaling to agree with the normalization used in Lemma A.5, correctly identifies cross-entropy, and makes the revised theorem's mixture assumptions explicit. These improve mathematical clarity and consistency. The gain is limited: the more specific assumptions are not reflected in the unchanged headline claims, and the rewritten proof retains notation inconsistencies, including ending with D1 where its setup concerns Dp.
